1. Central idea

The proposed method is a direct epigraph/active-constraint optimizer for the original evaluator objective. Instead of smoothing the max over shifts with a soft-max and accepting a surrogate optimum, introduce a raw objective variable τ and exact raw score variables so that the problem is locally formulated as a nonconvex constrained program with variables

    z = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_{n-1}, τ)

and exact constraints forcing τ to stay below every finite-support correlation score of h against 1-h. A local equality-preserving solver then makes an exact objective move under constraints corresponding to the actual maximum, rather than an approximation blended over every lag. This is different from the supplied parent program in two substantive ways:

- The true max is encoded structurally through nonconvex inequality constraints τ ≤ S_k(h). The local search targets the actual max set more directly than previous log-sum-exp smoothing, gradient/momentum statistics, and independent pending pair operations.
